alternatives.reason_rejected: It duplicates canonical state and can drift from JSONL.

rationale: JSONL is the preferred canonical machine-readable format; a generated Markdown copy would duplicate state and create synchronization risk.
summary: Store material decisions and milestones only in the target logs/ships_log.jsonl file and render it through QuarterDeck.
title: Use JSONL-only Ship's Log persistence

alternatives.option: Keep specs/001-drydock/spec.md and separate coverage checklist
alternatives.reason_rejected: The files duplicate authority and make completion state harder to review.

rationale: A single current specification removes competing behavior authorities, while stateful Soundings rows make task completion and acceptance evidence explicit and reviewable.
summary: Use docs/Drydock_Specification.md as the sole approved behavior specification and docs/SOUNDINGS.md as the authoritative implementation acceptance checklist; expose owned docs through QuarterDeck.
title: Make Drydock Specification and Soundings the development authorities

alternatives.option: Deploy to all target projects now
alternatives.reason_rejected: The decision workflow and backend have not yet been validated through Ed's own work.

rationale: Ship's Log remains an intended standard Drydock capability that will automatically capture design decisions for downstream publishing, but deploying it broadly before Ed validates the workflow would harden an unproven contract.
summary: Use Drydock's injected agent process as the proving ground for automatic decision capture; defer standard target-project deployment until the decision backend and workflow are validated.
title: Defer deployed Ship's Log capture while proving it in Drydock
